lesson.title: Question-Word Twins
lesson.subtitle: où ↔ ubiquitous, pourquoi ↔ wherefore, quand, comment, combien — the cognate question words.

hook.title: Every Question Word Has an English Cousin
hook.content: French's six question words all map to Latinate roots in English: où ('where' ↔ ubiquitous), quand ('when' ↔ quando), comment ('how' ↔ manner -ment), combien ('how much/many'), pourquoi ('why' ↔ wherefore), and quel/quelle ('which/what' ↔ quality)!

footnotes.title: Why quel, quelle, quels, quelles all sound like /kɛl/
footnotes.content: Even though quel agrees in writing with its noun (Quel train ? Quelle heure ?), all four forms sound 100% identical (/kɛl/)!

pattern.title: Question Word + est-ce que, or Short Inversion (Quelle heure est-il ?)
pattern.content: Pair question words with est-ce que or short être inversions.
pattern.linguist_note: Interrogative determiner quel agrees in gender and number with its head noun.
pattern.trap_note: Don't forget the grave accent on où ('where') — without the accent, ou means 'or'!

exercises.prompt: Match each French question word with its English cognate clue:
exercises.target_answer: ubiquitous (Latin ubi), quality (Latin qualis), manner (-ment adverb), wherefore (for-what), how-well (com + bien)
exercises.meaning: où (where), quel / quelle (which / what), comment (how), pourquoi (why), combien (how much / many)
exercises.explanation: Every French question word links back to a Latin root you already know.

exercises.prompt: French où ('where', from Latin ubi) shares its root with which English adjective meaning 'present everywhere at once'?
exercises.explanation: Latin ubīque ('everywhere') gave English ubiquitous; Latin ubi gave French où.

exercises.prompt: Because 'l'heure' ('the hour/time') is feminine, how do you write 'What time is it?'
exercises.meaning: What time is it? (lit. Which hour is it?)
exercises.explanation: heure is feminine, so quel becomes Quelle heure.

exercises.idea: when are you going to arrive (informal tu, using est-ce que)
cues: you are going to arrive → tu vas arriver
exercises.target_answer: Quand est-ce que tu vas arriver
exercises.meaning: When are you going to arrive?
exercises.explanation: Quand + est-ce que + tu vas arriver.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Comment est-ce que tu vas à la gare
exercises.target_answer: Comment est-ce que tu vas à la gare
exercises.meaning: How are you going to the station?
cues: you go to the station: tu vas à la gare
exercises.affirmation: You paired Comment with est-ce que cleanly.

summary.outcome: Deploy où, quand, comment, combien, pourquoi, and quel/quelle across real questions.

use_example.german: Quelle heure est-il et quand est-ce qu'on part ?
use_example.english: What time is it and when are we leaving?

summary.takeaway: où = ubiquitous, quel = quality, pourquoi = wherefore.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([8] The -eur Bridge): see how Question-Word Twins leads directly into The -eur Bridge.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "When are you going to arrive" in French:
twist.target_answer: Quand est-ce que tu vas arriver
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Quand est-ce que tu vas arriver" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of Question-Word Twins.

où.etymology_derivation: Latin ubi 'where' — the root English borrowed wholesale in 'ubiquitous' (present everywhere).

pourquoi.etymology_derivation: pour + quoi = 'for what' — English's 'wherefore' (for-what) built the same way: wherefore art thou.

quand.etymology_derivation: Latin quandō. In liaison before a vowel, the d sounds like /t/: quand il arrive /kɑ̃.t‿il/.

combien.etymology_derivation: When followed by a noun, takes bare de: combien de temps ('how much time').

quel.etymology_derivation: Agrees with its noun: quel (m), quelle (f), quels (mpl), quelles (fpl) — all four sound identical (/kɛl/)!

parce_que.etymology_derivation: Pourquoi asks 'for what?'; parce que answers 'by that which'.

heure.etymology_derivation: Latin hōra. Silent H triggers elision: l'heure.
